chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Ali (peace be upon him) assumed authority, he ascended the pulpit, praised Allah, and extolled Him. Then he said: 'By Allah, I will not give you more than your due from your spoils of war, not even a single dirham, as long as I have a palm tree left in Yathrib. So be truthful to yourselves. Do you see that I am withholding from myself what I shall give to you?' Aqeel stood up and said to him: 'By Allah, will you make me equal to a black man of Medina?' He said: 'Sit down. Is there no one else here to speak? And your preference over him is only by precedence or by piety.'

key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: A silver coin, used here to denote a small amount or even one's full due
key_terms.سَابِقَةٌ: Precedence, specifically in accepting Islam or performing good deeds
key_terms.عَقِيلٌ: Aqeel ibn Ali, the brother of Imam Ali
key_terms.فَيْئٌ: Spoils of war or war booty
key_terms.يَثْرِبَ: Yathrib, the former name of Medina

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about fairness and favoritism when he became the ruler?
ai.summary: This hadith captures Imam Ali’s (as) inaugural sermon, where he famously declared his personal austerity in war spoils ('fay') to demonstrate impartiality, asserting that distinction is based solely on piety or precedence in Islam rather than kinship. The narrative highlights the political tension with his cousin Aqeel, who challenged this meritocratic stance, underscoring the Shia emphasis on spiritual and moral superiority over tribal privilege. This event serves as a foundational model for just governance, illustrating the leader's duty to prioritize public equity over familial favoritism.
